H: boot (mount core, land on page or onboarding)
N: warm (prefetch a main page, mounted but dormant; needs user trigger)
T: bind view (to page name or kind), returns unbind
TT: fault class; static UGHH(fault) returns a plain-language message for the fault code (generic text for anything else)

Context.HSA: data (games: { GHA: id, GSU: game view })

Onboarding.OUG: done (finishing needs a profile; a missing profile reopens onboarding)

Events.SGGO: anything about the active profile changed (profile view, or null)
Events.AHAO: a write to storage failed (id, error)
Events.SUOA: game installed or replaced (install result + game view)
Events.SSNU: game log line (id, level, message, time)
Events.SSUH: free space level changed (level, quota, usage)
Events.OSGA: persistent storage was granted or lost (persisted)
Events.OOHT: a stored setting changed in another tab or here (key)

Scope.TA: timeout (fn, ms) -> cancel; deferred while dormant, fires on wake
Scope.TN: interval (fn, ms) -> cancel; stopped unless live or idle
Scope.TG: frame (fn, fps) -> cancel; core ticker, runs only while live
Scope.TO: listen (target, type, fn, options) -> cancel; dropped unless live or idle

Throttle.UAS: unmount halted main pages unused for ms (300000)
Throttle.UNS: max halted main pages kept warm (2)

OATU: register a fault table (code -> message, codes must be new)
GGHU: true when a real user input happened recently (or the trigger requirement is off)

GAHO.HHSA: mount the profile core (resolves when profiles are loaded)
GAHO.OUAN: true when an active profile exists
GAHO.HOTH: create the profile and make it active; refused with H87 when this Hangouts already has one
GAHO.GUHO: edit the active profile (name, username, bio, picture)
GAHO.NTGH: delete the profile and all of its game data, clips and caches (no arguments)
GAHO.NUGG: per-game stats of the active profile (all, or one game id)
GAHO.NHST: add playtime for a game (game id, game name, seconds, launched, profile id)
GAHO.ONHH: record an achievement (game id, game name, achievement, profile id); false if already earned
GAHO.TTGT: per-profile document store for a namespace (namespace, profile id) -> { get, put, delete, keys }
GAHO.UHSG: storage namespace prefix for a game under a profile (game id, profile id)
GAHO.TNNT: erase a profile's data for one game, or all games (profile id, game id)
GAHO.UOGO: register an async check run before a profile is deleted or overwritten; may veto by throwing; returns remover
GAHO.HTNT: import a profile file (blob, file, text); refused with H87 unless options.THHA replaces the existing profile and erases its data
GAHO.TTOO: promise that resolves when every queued write is durable
GAHO.note: one profile per Hangouts: there is no switching and no profile list

SHGA.NTSA: mount the package core (resolves when installed games are loaded)
SHGA.HOUG: installed games as views, sorted by name
SHGA.GTSO: one installed game view, or null
SHGA.AOTH: parse a .hngts without installing -> handle (blob, file, buffer, or an array of .hngts.partN files joined in order); refuses non-zip content (H58), oversize (H53) and cancelled (H86) before unpacking; ignores OS junk (__MACOSX, .DS_Store) and unwraps a single wrapping folder; a plain-data manifest is read without running any code, anything else runs in a network-locked worker; the handle says how it relates to the installed copy (USHO) and what changed (HNGN)
SHGA.GTUU: install a .hngts or an inspected handle; needs a user trigger; refuses to overwrite unless replace; an older version needs GNAG; identical content is a no-op (SAOU in the result) unless OSUH; the previous version is kept for rollback (the last 2)
SHGA.TAAN: remove a game and its page; optionally wipe every profile's data for it; needs a user trigger
SHGA.OGUH: stored html + assets + manifest of an installed game (used by the player) plus how it runs
SHGA.NOAT: build a .hngts blob from { manifest, html, assets: [{ path, data }] }
SHGA.UNTT: rebuild the .hngts of an installed game
SHGA.UNNO: register an async check run before a game is replaced or removed (game id, reason); returns remover
SHGA.HNTO: resolve a reference (relative, root-absolute, ./, Source/, Assets/-less) to an asset path in a map
SHGA.SUNA: game id for a game name
SHGA.NHGA: promise that resolves when every queued install/uninstall is done
SHGA.SSGO: install several at once (array or FileList of files/blobs/handles; .hngts.partN files are grouped by name); needs one user trigger; one failure never stops the rest -> [{ HHGS index, OUGU name, STSH ok, HASO install result or null, ATOH fault code or null, HOTA fault detail }]; up to 50 per call
SHGA.UUHS: roll back to an earlier kept version (game id, { NANG: version or stamp }); needs a user trigger; the current version becomes the newest kept version
SHGA.NGOS: verify an installed game against its stored fingerprint and confirm its kept versions exist -> { OGHN ok, TUOU installed before fingerprints existed, ONAS problems }
SHGA.USHG: set how a game runs (game id, TUSU sandbox or SGGA full); needs a user trigger; refused while the game runs
SHGA.THAU: open the file picker (multiple by default) and install or, with GTOG, only inspect; needs a user trigger; .hngts.partN files are grouped; one failure never stops the rest
SHGA.TUHN: bind drag and drop on an element (element, { NASN hover fn, OTSH done fn, GTOG inspect only, install options }) -> unbind
SHGA.AAHO: compare two version texts (semantic versions with prerelease order, otherwise natural order) -> -1, 0, 1

ONHN.GHSO: start a game for the profile inside options.box (default body); needs a user trigger; one game at a time; runs sandboxed unless the game was granted full access
ONHN.NTGA: stop a game (default the running one) -> { id, elapsed seconds }
ONHN.GSNO: id of the running game, or null
ONHN.UTNN: view of the running session, or null: { GSAH, OUGU, HNHA, TOGO iframe, NUNU ready promise, OOSS start, STUO mode, GGAT needs full access }
ONHN.GGUA: captured console/error lines of the running session (last 400)
ONHN.OGUN: player settings (partial in, full out; reading needs no trigger): UUGH clip on or off (default on), TAAO clip key as a KeyboardEvent code (default F9), plus timing settings; clip settings are saved and shared between tabs
ONHN.ATNA: save the last 10 to 20 seconds of the running game as a clip (needs a user trigger); the game frame also does it on the clip key -> clip meta
ONHN.AASH: clip metas of the profile, newest first (optionally one game id)
ONHN.TGUO: a clip by id -> meta + blob
ONHN.OHSA: delete a clip (needs a user trigger)
ONHN.THHS: delete every clip of the profile, or of one game (needs a user trigger)
ONHN.ATTG: fullscreen the running game (needs a user trigger)
ONHN.clips: Clip is the only capture: the game frame keeps two staggered recorders (canvas plus game audio), so at any moment one holds 10 to 20 seconds; pressing Clip stops the oldest, saves it to the games database (webm, duration fixed in the header) and starts a fresh one. Games without a canvas, or with clips turned off, give H92 and H93. At most 24 clips per game and 512 MB per profile; the oldest go first

Fields.GSAH: identity (profile id, game id, achievement id)
Fields.SNTS: picture (blob; input also takes a data url)
Fields.OUNU: object url for a picture or icon
Fields.TTAH: icon (blob; in a manifest, an asset path)

Options.UOTO: export/import: include per-game documents and localStorage (default true)
Options.THHA: import: overwrite an existing profile with the same username
Options.UNOU: install: replace an installed game with the same id
Options.UTOO: uninstall: also erase every profile's data for the game
Options.AANS: inspect/install: callback with { phase, done, total }; a batch install adds HHGS (the item index)
Options.SGTU: launch: element that receives the game frame
Options.UUOA: player: how often (ms) playtime is flushed to the profile (default 30000)
Options.STHH: player: ready fallback (ms) if the game never finishes loading (default 15000)
Options.SOUH: inspect/install/download: AbortSignal; aborting stops the work and refuses with H86
Options.GNAG: install: allow an older version over a newer one
Options.OSUH: install: rewrite even when the content is identical
Options.NANG: rollback: the version or stamp to restore
Options.GTOG: pick/drop: inspect only, do not install

Handle.HGAG: [{ path, blob }] every file under Source/ except H26.html, typed by extension
Handle.AHHT: poster blob (manifest.poster is an asset path)
Handle.THGU: achievement icon blobs by achievement id
Handle.OAAH: already installed: { version, updated } or null
Handle.GSHU: the reference that did not resolve
Handle.USHO: relation to the installed copy: ONAA new, GSST same content, SGHO same version but different content, GAUA newer, UTUN older
Handle.HNGN: against the installed copy: { HOOU size change in bytes, AUAG achievements added, TNGA achievements removed } or null
Handle.AGGU: content fingerprint (path, size and crc of every file)

GameView.OUTO: install result: an existing game was replaced

Session.HNHA: profile id the session is bound to
Session.NUNU: promise: the game document finished loading
Session.TUSG: log level (log, info, warn, error, debug)

Bridge.OHAN: save data (json text on save, parsed value on load)
Bridge.GNTA: per-launch config variable in the frame
Bridge.game api: window.Hangouts.unlock(id) / save(data) / load() in every game; promises; unlock and save resolve true or false

Storage.databases: two IndexedDB databases: zero.hangouts (everything Hangouts itself needs) and zero.games (everything games write); Hangouts One uses its own names so the two never share data
Storage.zero.hangouts.meta: key -> value: active (profile id), onb (onboarding), erase (profile ids whose game data is still being erased), persist, cdnrepo, playcfg ([clip on, clip key])
Storage.zero.hangouts.games: one record per installed game (manifest, sizes, package stamp, fingerprint AGGU, how it runs SNSA, kept earlier versions OSAA)
Storage.zero.hangouts.packages: one record per installed or kept package (html + assets), key game:stamp
Storage.zero.hangouts.cdn: catalog and hero (cached listing) and map:<catalog id> (which catalog entry became which installed game)
Storage.zero.games.data: one row per value, key [game, profile, namespace, key]; namespaces: d documents (Hangouts.data and save), l localStorage of the game, r registry of the game's own indexedDB names (full access only)
Storage.zero.games.cache: the game cache (Hangouts.cache): key [game, profile, key]; value, size, write time, expiry; per game and profile 64 MB and 4096 keys, 32 MB per value, ttl up to a year; over the limit the oldest write goes first; expired entries are dropped on read, on write and at start; uninstalling a game or deleting the profile empties it
Storage.zero.games.clips: clips: id, game, profile, time, duration, mime, size, size, width, height and the video blob
Storage.zero.games.usage: bytes and row count per [game, profile]
Storage.zero.games.sections: one row per game: created, last write, total bytes, optional limit override
Storage.raw storage: full-access games only: their own indexedDB databases and Cache API caches stay physically separate but namespaced per profile and game (prefix + profile:game:) and each database name is registered in the games database so it can always be found and erased. Sandboxed games have no indexedDB or Cache API (they get SecurityError and are flagged as needing full access); localStorage, Hangouts.data and Hangouts.cache work everywhere
Storage.writes: every change is one atomic transaction that merges into the stored record (read-modify-write), so two tabs can never overwrite each other with a stale copy; profiles, saves and settings use strict durability
Storage.limits: per game section default min(512 MB, 20% of quota), adjustable per game with SetLimit; localStorage emulation 64 MB per game and profile; documents 16 MB json or 256 MB binary per value, 100000 keys per game and profile; game writes are refused when free space would drop below max(64 MB, 3% of quota) so the Hangouts database always has room; installs need their size plus 12.5% plus 16 MB free
Storage.never automatic: nothing is deleted to make room except the game cache (oldest write first, inside its own limit); saves and clips are only removed by the user or by their own caps
Storage.tabs: BroadcastChannel zero.sync announces changes (kinds p profile, g games, m meta, c catalog map, d game data); receivers reload from the database, and a wake (focus, visibility, online, pageshow) reloads everything as a fallback
Storage.locks: zero.play.<game>.<profile> is held while a game runs (one tab at a time per game and profile; profile delete, uninstall, replace, rollback and access changes refuse while held elsewhere); zero.tab.<id> counts open tabs

Faults.note: one list, H1 to H94. H1-H14 pages and routing, H15-H37 core engine and storage errors, H38-H47 profile and data, H48-H58 package, H59-H61 player, H63 play settings, H64-H71 catalog, H72-H77 storage limits, tabs and game endpoints, H82 format, H84 reserved publisher name, H85 not released yet, H86 cancelled, H87 profile exists, H88 older version, H89 no earlier version, H90 needs newer Hangouts, H92 nothing to record, H93 clips off, H94 unknown clip. H62 and H78-H81, H83, H91 are retired
Faults.H53: package too large (bytes, entry count, or file size)
Faults.message: Hangouts.TT.UGHH(fault) -> a plain-language message for any fault code

TSAS: run an async chain that started from a real user input; gated calls inside it (install, launch) stay allowed for up to 10 minutes

OHTH.UANO: catalog { list, time, stale } (cached in memory for 10 minutes, then refreshed in the background; options.UUTU refetches; offline answers instantly from the saved copy with stale true and refreshes when the browser comes back online)
OHTH.GAHN: sync snapshot of the loaded catalog
OHTH.ONHU: download + verify one game (catalog id) -> blob; options.progress
OHTH.UTTT: download, verify, install (needs a user input); parts download in parallel (3), each part fails over across mirrors and is checked against its own hash when the catalog has one; two calls for the same game share one download; an older catalog version replaces a newer installed one (the catalog wins)
OHTH.NTOA: play a catalog game: installs first if absent, never needs the network if installed; options.update also updates; options.box
OHTH.UHOS: repo, idle timeout, ready wait (partial in, full out); the repo must be gh/owner/name@ref on jsDelivr
OHTH.STTU: resolve a catalog path to the current jsDelivr mirror url
OHTH.GSHG: catalog games that have an update (the same views as UANO)
OHTH.AHNG: update every catalog game that has an update, one after another (needs a user trigger; options.SOUH aborts) -> [{ HHGS index, GSAH, STSH ok, HASO, ATOH }]

Catalog.TTTU: true when served from the offline cache
Catalog.HONH: ANGN not installed, UAAA installed, HSAU installed but the catalog has a different sha/version
Catalog.NOAA: installed game id (may differ from the catalog id)
Catalog.GTHN: launch option: update first if the catalog changed
Catalog.HONO: setting: abort a download that stalls this long (ms)
Catalog.repo: the official Hangouts repository, served only through jsDelivr (never raw.githubusercontent). Its address, hosts and file paths are stored encoded in the app (not readable in the bundle). Change it with Cdn.Tune({ repo })
Catalog.layout: metadata/metadata.txt (the catalog; metadata/catalog.json also read), metadata/media/posters/<Title>.png (covers), metadata/media/screenshots/<Title>/1.png ... (at least 3 per game for the Store page), legal.txt, seasons/<season>/legal.txt, seasons/<season>/<category>/<id>/game.hngts (or game.hngts.part1..n)
Catalog.catalog file: a JSON list of games, or { seasons: [{ id, name }], games: [...] }. Fetched first, cached for offline use
Catalog.seasons: a game season comes from the catalog; the catalog file may set defaultSeason (default manifesto)
Catalog.categories: the defaults are originals, essentials and socials; a catalog file may add categories with categories: [{ id, name }]. Locals are uploads on this device: never in the repo, never published, no season
Catalog.entry: { id, title, subtitle, studio (creator is accepted too), version, description, season, category, poster, screenshots (gallery is accepted too), hngts (optional, defaults to the folder's game.hngts), sha256 (required unless soon), soon, featured, tagline, added, seal }
Catalog.originals: an Originals entry, or any entry under the reserved creator, is listed only with a valid team seal over id, version, sha256, creator, season and category (H26-ENTRY-2); otherwise it is hidden and counted in Hidden
Catalog.OHTH.HGGT: () [{ id, name, subtitle, number, count, categories: [{ id, name, count }] }]
Catalog.OHTH.UHTA: () the three repo categories plus Locals (local: true)
Catalog.OHTH.GHHH: () every installed game with its category and season; anything not from the repo is a Local with no season
Catalog.OHTH.UNNS: (season) { root, season } the legal notices, empty text when a notice does not exist
Catalog.OHTH.UANO: ({ refresh, season, category }) { list, time, stale, hidden }
Catalog.season: a game's season is assigned only by the team in the repo metadata, normally by date; it is never read from a package. The catalog's seasons list gives each season { id, name, subtitle, number }, e.g. Manifesto (Season One)
Catalog.soon: soon: true lists a game with its details before it exists. It has no sha256 or files, shows state soon and cannot be installed or launched (H85). Coming-soon entries under the official repo do not need a seal
Catalog.screenshots: the tools warn when a game has fewer than 3 (publish.py --require-screenshots and check-catalog --strict refuse it); Hangouts lists it anyway
Catalog.entry extras: bytes (optional total size; the space check runs before downloading) and partSha (optional sha256 per part, same order as hngts)
Catalog.access: catalog installs of originals and essentials run with full access; every other category starts sandboxed

SSTG.note: the core engine is private; it is only reachable when the page is opened with #bare (no boot, used by the tests); Hangouts.ANAG then exposes the storage internals the tests use
SSTG.NNNO: provide an rpc handler (name, fn, { limit, cache })
SSTG.ONUG: call an rpc handler (name, payload, options); cached and rate-limited when the handler asks

HNSG.H: read a .hngts or any zip (blob, total byte limit, progress) -> files; stored and deflate entries

Format.version: format 1. Readers accept a missing format field as 1 and refuse anything newer with H82
Format.extension: .hngts (a zip; any case; stored or deflate entries)
Format.H26/H26.js: definition: Hangouts.define({ format, id, name, description, creator, version, category, tags, license, poster, gallery, achievements, x-* }); the forms define(...) and Define(...) also work
Format.Source/Assets/**: everything else the game loads, addressed relative to the page
Format.H26/Signature.json: optional seal { v: 1, alg: ES256, kid, sig }; required only when the creator is a reserved name
Format.identity: id is the game's identity (lowercase letters, digits and single dashes, up to 64). Without one it is derived from the name. Pin it: renaming an unpinned game changes its id and orphans its saves
Format.extension fields: keys beginning x- are kept through installs (up to 16 KB in total); other unknown keys are dropped
Format.limits: 20000 entries, 1 GiB in total, page up to 256 MiB, definition up to 256 KiB, 200 achievements, 50 gallery images, 12 tags
Format.store catalog: catalog.json entries point at a package with the field hngts (one path or url, or an ordered array of parts) and must carry its sha256; entries without a valid sha256 are dropped; entries under a reserved creator must also carry a valid seal
Format.import: a File not named *.hngts is refused with H58; any blob that is not a zip is refused with H58; parts named *.hngts.partN are joined in order (gaps refuse with H48); blobs are judged by their content
Format.manifest extras: access (sandbox or full request), changelog (text, 4000), homepage (https link), minApi (integer; higher than this Hangouts gives H90); keys beginning x- are kept through installs (up to 16 KB in total)
Format.versions: versions compare as semantic versions (prerelease order included) and fall back to natural order; installing an older version needs options GNAG; identical content is skipped; the last 2 earlier versions are kept for Rollback; Verify checks the stored copy against its fingerprint

NNGA.TUSN: { persisted, quota, usage, free, reserve, level ok|low|critical, profiles, installed, package bytes, per-game sections with bytes, limit and per-profile use, orphans, ATAN cache and clip usage { HOUA cache bytes, GUTO cache entries, OATO clips, GAHA clip bytes }, live sync }
NNGA.HTHA: ask the browser to keep the data (needs a user input in some browsers); true when persistent
NNGA.UGSG: re-check free space now and emit a pressure event when the level changed
NNGA.GONO: (game id, bytes | null): change one game's storage limit (needs a user input)
NNGA.GTOT: catalog-installed games that can be removed and downloaded again, least recently played first; their saves are not touched by uninstalling
NNGA.SATO: check the games database counters; { fix: true } repairs the counters only, never data
NNGA.AAHH: data sections of games that are not installed, sections of missing profiles, stray or broken game records
NNGA.AHOO: reload profiles, games and settings from storage now
NNGA.OSUO: resolves when every background write has finished
NNGA.ASSN: delete every game cache entry, or one game's (needs a user trigger); saves and clips are untouched

GameSdk.where: window.Hangouts inside every game frame; every call returns a promise; failures are Error objects with .code (a fault code) and .name HangoutsError
GameSdk.Hangouts.game: { id, name, version, mode } where mode is sandbox or full
GameSdk.Hangouts.player: snapshot { playerId, username, name, bio, avatar (blob url or null) }; playerId is anonymous and different for every game, stable per profile and game; the internal profile id is never exposed
GameSdk.Hangouts.data: get(key), set(key, value), remove(key), keys(prefix?), clear(), usage() -> { used, limit, keys, game }; values are json, Blob, ArrayBuffer or typed arrays; stored in this game's section for the current profile
GameSdk.Hangouts.save(value) / load(): one json save slot on top of data (resolves true or false / the value or null)
GameSdk.Hangouts.achievements: list() -> [{ id, name, description, icon, unlocked, time }], unlock(id) -> true the first time, has(id)
GameSdk.Hangouts.unlock(id): shortcut for achievements.unlock that resolves false instead of rejecting
GameSdk.Hangouts.stats.get(): { playtime seconds, launches, first, last } for this game and profile
GameSdk.Hangouts.storage.estimate(): { used, limit, keys, game, pressure } for this game
GameSdk.Hangouts.on(event, fn): returns an off function; events: profile (snapshot when the player edits the profile), stopping (async handler, up to 1.5 s to save before the frame is removed), storage (pressure level changes), storageerror ({ code } when a background localStorage write could not be stored)
GameSdk.localStorage: works as usual and persists to the games database (64 MB per game and profile, QuotaExceededError when exceeded); sessionStorage stays in memory; indexedDB and caches are namespaced per profile and game
GameSdk.limits: 400 request burst refilling at 200 per second (H75), unknown endpoints get H76, malformed arguments H46, oversized values H45, storage limit H73, storage full H72
GameSdk.security: only the running game's own frame is answered; a game can only reach its own section for the profile it was launched with; no profile ids, no other profiles, no other games, nothing destructive
GameSdk.Hangouts.cache: get(key) -> value or undefined, put(key, value, { ttl seconds }) -> { size, expires }, has(key), stat(key) -> { size, updated, expires } or null, remove(key) -> bool, keys(prefix?), clear(), usage() -> { used, limit, keys, maxKeys }; values are json, Blob, ArrayBuffer or typed arrays; a cache is for things a game can rebuild, Hangouts may drop entries at any time (oldest write first over the limit, and after ttl); reads never extend life
GameSdk.clip: the clip key (F9 by default) works inside the game; games do not call it and cannot read clips

Security.isolation: a game runs in an iframe without allow-same-origin (sandbox): an opaque origin, so it cannot read Hangouts' databases, profile, tokens or other games' data, and cannot reach the parent page. Its files reach it as blob urls the frame builds itself; Hangouts talks to it only through the message bridge
Security.full access: games that need indexedDB or the Cache API (engines such as Unity, Emscripten IDBFS, Eaglercraft) are flagged (GGAT) and can be granted full access: the same-origin frame the older builds always used. A full-access game can read Hangouts' storage, so it is only granted by the user (Grant) or to catalog originals and essentials
Security.manifest access: manifest.access may ask for full; it changes nothing until the user grants it
Security.reserved names: the creator name teamhangouts is reserved. Case, spacing, punctuation, digit and symbol swaps, look-alike letters, full-width forms and hidden characters are all folded away before comparing, and any creator that contains it is reserved
Security.seal: a package under a reserved creator is accepted only with H26/Signature.json: an ES256 signature (P-256, SHA-256) over the sorted list of every other entry's path and SHA-256. Anything else is refused with H84
Security.keys and names: the public keys (HHHO) and the reserved names (TSNT) are build-time configuration next to the package core; with no keys the reserved name is refused everywhere (fails closed); catalog entries of the seal categories (originals) need a seal too
Security.gating: every call that changes profiles, installs, removes, tunes, grants, clips or registers a guard needs a recent real user input in Hangouts itself (H10); input inside a game frame never counts (the clip key is the one exception, and it can only save a clip)
Security.manifests: a plain-data manifest is read without running code; a script manifest runs in a worker with fetch, WebSocket, XMLHttpRequest, importScripts and storage removed
Security.limit: the seal only stops other people using the name inside Hangouts; anyone can still write their own launcher

UNNH.note: Hangouts.UNNH backs the Today page. It never waits on the network: it answers from memory or the cached catalog at once and refreshes the catalog in the background (at most once a minute), then emits OUTA so the page can ask again
UNNH.SGOT: ({ refresh }) { hero: up to 5 items, continue: EVERY installed game the profile can pick up again (played, or holding a save), newest first, each with playtime, sessions, last played, TANN save bytes and ASAG/NUSA achievements, shelves: [...], installed, stale, hidden, offline, time }
UNNH.item: { id (catalog id, or the game id for a local), game (installed id or null), name, category, categoryName, season, poster (url, installed cover preferred), source store|local, state absent|here|update|local, creator, version, description, tagline, featured, added, play (seconds), count, last }
UNNH.TSTH: (id, { box, update }) plays an installed game, or installs it from the catalog first (needs a user input)
UNNH.catalog fields: an entry may carry featured (true), tagline (text) and added (unix seconds); publish.py sets added
UNNH.event: OUTA fires when playtime, the library, the profile or the catalog changed; not while a game is running (it fires once when the game stops)

Quiet.while a game runs: no timers except the 30 second playtime save and one 60 second page timer; catalog refreshes and window-focus resyncs are held back and run once when the game stops; changes from other tabs to games or the catalog are applied then too (profile and setting changes still apply at once); the html element gets the attribute NGNS so the UI can pause its own animations
Quiet.ONHN.NNTH: () true while a game is running

Interface.font: Hangouts: Geist (SIL Open Font License, copyright kept in the file) renamed and embedded as one variable font covering weights 100 to 900. The standalone static set (Hangouts.otf = Regular, Hangouts-Thin.otf ... Hangouts-Black.otf) is in Fonts/
Interface.background: #000000 on html, body and every page
Interface.sidebar: one logo (top) and four buttons in the middle: Today, Store, Library, Profile. Each opens its real page instance through Hangouts.G. Icons are Gravity UI and the logo is H26.svg, embedded as one inline symbol sprite (nothing is fetched). Hover is gray, the current page is white (no highlight shape), pressing shrinks the button by 2 px slowly (360 ms in, 620 ms out) for a weighted feel
Interface.behaviour: the button for the current page is marked (aria-current); game pages under Store:<id> keep Store marked; the sidebar hides on onboarding and slides away while a game runs; arrow keys, Home and End move between buttons; the sidebar always stays on screen at the same distance from the left edge and only shrinks (down to 70%) when the window is short. There are no tooltips for now
Interface.names: every class, custom property and attribute in the stylesheet uses the same lexicon codes as the code, so the CSS is obfuscated exactly like the JS
Interface.test mode: the interface is not built in #bare test mode

Kit.what: the UI kit every page is built from: native CSS and JS, no framework, every class, custom property, keyframe and attribute in the H26 alphabet (the build refuses anything else). Source: src/kit.css and src/K.tpl.js. Pages call it directly from inside the bundle
Kit.tokens: CSS custom properties: colors (Bg #000000, Panel, Raised, Lift, Line, Edge, Text, Muted, Hover gray, Faint, Accent, Danger, Good, Warn), radii R1-R4 and Pill, spacing S1-S7 (4 to 48 px), motion (Fast 120, Base 208, Slow 280 ms, one Ease curve), Shadow. Change a look by changing a token, never a component
Kit.type: Title 28/700, Head 16/600, Body 14, Note 13 muted, Caption 12/600, buttons and fields 13; font Hangouts
Kit.layout: Stack (column) and Row with a gap option, Card, Sheet (page-in animation: fade and 0.3% scale over 280 ms), Empty
Kit.actions: Button (kinds: soft, primary, ghost, danger; sizes small, large; icon-only when it has no label; block; busy shows a spinner), Chip (toggle), Segmented (sliding indicator, arrow keys), Menu (anchored popover: arrows, Home, End, Escape, returns the chosen value), Dialog, Alert, Confirm (danger confirms focus Cancel), Prompt, Toast (polite live region, at most 3)
Kit.inputs: Field (label bound to input, hint, Warn() for errors), Select, Check, Radio, Switch (native inputs), Range
Kit.content: Tile (3:4 poster, subtle hover zoom as in the Experiment, badge, lazy image with initial fallback), Shelf (title, arrows, edge fades, drag to scroll with a mouse), Carousel (dots with a progress fill driven by CSS, swipe and drag, arrow keys, pauses on hover, focus and hidden tab), Badge, Avatar, Progress (determinate or idle), Spinner, Skeleton
Kit.rules: everything is keyboard reachable with a white focus ring; dialogs make the page behind inert and restore focus; text is always set with textContent; motion respects prefers-reduced-motion and pauses while a game runs; icons are Gravity UI in one inline sprite (Icon(name))
Kit.lists: Item (lead, title, note, end controls), Group (a card of Items), Grid (auto-fill columns), Section (heading, note, content), Stat (big number and label), Picker (a field-style button that opens a Menu; the choice updates at once)
Kit.shape: the blocky look: corners are squircles (corner-shape: squircle) on one four-step scale by role (R1 12, R2 18 for buttons, fields, chips and the segmented control, R3 24 for cards and menus, R4 32 for dialogs and big surfaces), so a control has the same radius at every size; avatars are full squircles; toggles, slider thumbs, radios, dots and bars stay round. No borders anywhere (gray backgrounds separate things), icons are Gravity UI and filled where a filled version exists
Kit.options: components take one options object; the keys are lexicon codes like everything else, see K.Api in the source for the list

Cores.HNAH: H26/<this>:<game id>: one non-persistent core per launched game (one non-persistent core is active at a time)

CoreDef.OHUH: assets [{ TGTT: src, HOTN: kind, UGTS: attributes }]
CoreDef.UGTO: persistent: stays mounted beside the active core
